:::{#thm-lotus}

#### Law of the Unconscious Statistician (LOTUS)

**Discrete case.**
For any function $g$ of a *discrete* random variable $X$:

$$\E{g(X)} = \sum_{x \in \rangef{X}} g(x) \cd \P(X=x)$$

**Continuous case.**
For any function $g$ of a *continuous* random variable $X$ with density $\p(X=x)$:

$$\E{g(X)} = \int_{x \in \rangef{X}} g(x) \cd \p(X=x)\, dx$$

:::

::: proof

We prove the discrete case.

Let $Y = g(X)$.
By @def-expectation applied to $Y$:

$$
\ba
\E{g(X)}
&= \E{Y} && \text{(substitution } Y = g(X) \text{)}
\\&= \sum_{y \in \rangef{Y}} y \cd \P(Y=y) && \text{(definition of expectation for discrete r.v.)}
\\&= \sum_{y \in \rangef{Y}} y \cd \P(g(X)=y) && \text{(substitute } Y = g(X) \text{ in probability expression)}
\\&= \sum_{y \in \rangef{Y}} y \cd \sum_{\substack{x \in \rangef{X} \\ g(x) = y}} \P(X=x) && \text{(law of total probability over } \{x : g(x) = y\} \text{)}
\\&= \sum_{x \in \rangef{X}} g(x) \cd \P(X=x) && \text{(rearrange double sum grouping by } g(x) \text{)}
\ea
$$

where the last equality follows by rearranging the double sum,
grouping each term $x$ by its image $y = g(x)$.

:::

::: notes

LOTUS says that to compute $\E{g(X)}$,
we do not need to first find the distribution of $g(X)$;
we can compute the expectation directly using the distribution of $X$.
The continuous case is the density-weighted analogue of this argument;
see rme's
[Probability chapter](https://morrison-lab.github.io/rme/chapters/probability.html#thm-lotus)
for the fully rigorous continuous-case proof, which relies on a
change-of-variables theorem beyond this page's scope.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-lotus}
#### Expected value of $X^2$ for a Bernoulli variable

Let $X \sim \Ber(\pi)$.
By LOTUS (@thm-lotus, discrete case):

$$
\ba
\E{X^2}
&= \sum_{x \in \set{0,1}} x^2 \cd \P(X=x)
&& \text{(LOTUS, discrete case)} \\
&= 0^2 \cd \P(X=0) + 1^2 \cd \P(X=1)
&& \text{(expand sum over } x = 0 \text{ and } x = 1 \text{)} \\
&= 0^2 \cd (1-\pi) + 1^2 \cd \pi
&& \text{(substitute Bernoulli PMF values)} \\
&= 0 + \pi
&& \text{(simplify each term)} \\
&= \pi
\ea
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-lotus-continuous}
#### Expected value of $X^2$ for a Uniform(0,1) variable

Let $X \sim \text{Uniform}(0,1)$, so $\p(X=x) = 1$ for $x \in [0,1]$.
By LOTUS (@thm-lotus, continuous case):

$$
\ba
\E{X^2}
&= \int_0^1 x^2 \cd \p(X=x)\,dx
&& \text{(LOTUS, continuous case)}
\\&= \int_0^1 x^2 \cd 1\,dx
&& \text{(}\p(X=x) = 1\text{ on } [0,1]\text{)}
\\&= \sb{\frac{x^3}{3}}_0^1
&& \text{(antiderivative of } x^2\text{)}
\\&= \frac{1}{3}.
&& \text{(evaluate at the bounds)}
\ea
$$

:::
